items.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And then I saw that you had done a date with Dannie Richmond, of course known with Charles Mingus. [INTERVIEWEE] No, but my revelation was we’re not [inaudible].

ctx.x: No, he was… He was… on some of the dates with Quincy, he played the drums. And when, with Peggy Lee. And when I talked too much, he said, “Hey, Tits, shut up and play your chrome sandwich.” That’s Grady. [laughs] See, you wanted anecdotes. You got it. “Hey, Tits. Shut up, man, and play your chrome sandwich.” So that’s Grady. That’s Grady. [laughs] I hope he’s okay, because he must be up in, in those numbers. Not far from mine. [laughs]
And then I saw that you had done a date with Dannie Richmond, of course known with Charles Mingus.
No, but my revelation was we’re not [inaudible].

items.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And Charlie Mingus played bass with that trio.

ctx.x: So Toots, when you say you were ill, what disease did you have?

Asthma and pneumonia. And I still have to be careful for asthma. In my life, I went through the total scope of asthma puffs and even… oh, that’s a beautiful anecdote. Even when I came to the States the first time. That was in ’47, with my uncle, the brother of my father. And we went… There was a club—The Embers. I wound up playing there with the George Shearing Quartet. And I went to listen. I knew all the records. I was up on all my bebop. And in the Embers restaurant, jazz place, there was the trio with Red…
